claims.claim: The IRS describes an LLC as a business structure allowed by state statute and identifies owners as members.

The management pattern of an LLC depends on applicable state law and its governing agreement; Delaware's statute defaults management to members unless the LLC agreement vests management in one or more managers.

Delaware law provides an example in which an LLC's debts and obligations are the LLC's and a member or manager is not personally liable solely for being a member or manager; the statute also permits a person to agree to personal liability.
The IRS states that federal tax classification for an LLC can depend on the number of members and elections, so a state-law LLC label does not by itself settle federal tax treatment.
A member may also be a manager, and an LLC may have more than one manager, under the Delaware statutory example.
Because LLC law is primarily state law and governing agreements can alter statutory defaults, a general lesson cannot determine authority or liability for a real LLC.
